[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday "converge" means arrive at the answer; numerically the vector only gets closer with each iteration and stops changing in the printed digits, never reaching the limit exactly.
[1] misconception (M) -> OneIterationSuffices: wrong rule: One vector-matrix multiplication gives the exact page ranks. Right rule: Accuracy grows with iterations: about 20 multiplications give two decimal places for tiny.txt and 20 more give three.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> OneIterationSuffices: Applies LT (run with T, then with more T, compare digits) unevenly: e.g. comparing a run with T = 20 to one with T = 21 and concluding that unchanged digits are accurate. (here mixing in: "One vector-matrix multiplication gives the exact page ranks")

[0] names_the_element (N): A performance measure: the number of iterations a method needs to reach a given number of accurate decimal places.
[1] states_the_rule (S): The power method needs about 20 multiplications for two decimal places and another 20 for three on tiny.txt, against tens of thousands and millions of moves for RandomSurfer; Brin and Page report 50 to 100 iterations for the web.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Run Markov with increasing T (20, 40, ...) and compare the printed vectors; the digits that stop changing are the converged ones.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Markov 20 and 40 agree to two decimals (0.27245 vs 0.27303) and the 40-iteration vector is accurate to three.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Each additional iteration shrinks the error by roughly a constant factor determined by the second largest eigenvalue of P, so a fixed number of iterations adds about one digit.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): T in Markov is the iteration count whose size the convergence rate fixes: about 20 per decimal digit for tiny.txt.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Choose the stopping point (iteration count) for an iterative method so that results are accurate to the needed digits without wasted work.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> OneIterationSuffices: Doubling T from 20 to 40 keeps the first two digits and adds one; changing the leap probability or the graph changes the rate (it depends on lambda2).
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use convergence measurements whenever an iterative or sampling method must be stopped; it explains why the power method (about 20 iterations per digit) is preferred to simulation (10x moves per digit).
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Enough iterations must be run for the required accuracy. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: T chosen too small (or a simulation with too few moves): printed digits look precise but are not accurate.

wrong: One vector-matrix multiplication gives the exact page ranks. | right: One multiplication gives only the probabilities after one move; the vector converges with repeated multiplication (for tiny.txt about 20 multiplications give two decimal places and about 40 give three).

The convergence rate counts how many power-method multiplications are needed for a given accuracy: about 20 for two decimal places and 20 more for three.
